requirements.requirement: Establish a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
requirements.summary: node1 was bootstrapped alone (cmd-35c7ab546ee240d1, cluster_size=1, Primary), seed data appdb.orders was created and populated (cmd-19a35fbba3f64878). node2 joined via mariabackup SST after resolving a wrong wsrep_provider path and an SELinux connectto denial, reaching cluster_size=2/Synced with the seed data present (cmd-32264348fc3f41a7, cmd-50ae845542304d29). node3 joined and reached cluster_size=3/Primary/Synced with the same data (cmd-e48f6c7145504504, cmd-94d9aa4bad754e8c). A cross-node write test (insert on node2, select on node3) confirmed multi-master replication before scale-out (cmd-a688bb4c03514a18, cmd-0cf0b57331104be2).

requirements.requirement: Add node4 as a fourth cluster member that carries the existing data
requirements.summary: node4 was installed, firewalled, and configured with the 4-node gcomm list (cmd-99bc13e1d5d84959, cmd-dc56ccc562174379, cmd-c86da4154b904863), and node1-3 configs were updated to include node4 (cmd-8f35e7224c6f4561, cmd-31276cd8e65e47b7, cmd-8dfad7cb865d41d8). After starting mariadb on node4 (cmd-ee6983533be94050), a direct query showed wsrep_cluster_size=4, status Synced, and all pre-existing seed/insert rows present (cmd-13d222fba14c4096), confirming the SST transferred existing data successfully.

requirements.requirement: node4 accepts writes like the other members
requirements.summary: An insert issued directly on node4 (cmd-13d222fba14c4096, item 'from-node4') was confirmed present on node1 shortly after (cmd-35bcc4c4666b49e1), directly demonstrating node4 accepts and replicates writes to the rest of the cluster.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: For each of node1-node4, the trace shows a pre-restart baseline boot_id and healthy Synced/size=4 state (cmd-9b2d7f816c5b417e, cmd-1d8540bcceed4b1c, cmd-f49f9271c63e480a, cmd-46799ef2b1f24ed6), a reboot acknowledgement followed by observed disconnection (cmd-7a6c769969a842f3/cmd-dbdde6ccbd3a44d9, cmd-083386a893444fa1/cmd-bdbf02038cc442a1, cmd-90b3d7d23be04a43/cmd-728055a8a35342eb, cmd-9905e73d779a46cf/cmd-62b19ddbb2584acd), a distinct post-restart boot_id (cmd-99de283fe1ca4e4b, cmd-74f136930c2f4907, cmd-0b25f0dff4874311, cmd-102e136abc4d49ad), and recovered service/cluster/data state with cluster_size=4, Primary, Synced, correct row count (cmd-acc34e78e4b0427b, cmd-b8fcac5d7464438f, cmd-57bb1b0a123a48e8, cmd-2c26e75f52d941d8). A final write on node4 replicating to node1 after all four restarts confirms end-to-end health (cmd-ab1e68567f0542a5, cmd-ef4c8cd5322f48c1). The fixed lifecycle before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate each boot_id transition for all four nodes.

overall_summary: The executor built a 3-node Galera cluster (node1-3) from scratch with seeded application data, verified multi-master write replication, then added node4 which received the existing data via SST and successfully accepted and replicated a write of its own — both material task outcomes are directly and coherently evidenced. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and consistently demonstrated across all four nodes, with boot-identity transitions cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good overall: blockers (wrong provider path, SELinux SST denial, a stale partial datadir) were diagnosed and fixed rather than worked around destructively, though one troubleshooting SELinux policy module was loaded and then reverted in favor of a boolean, and minor log-file residue was left in /tmp on all nodes.
limitations: No direct evidence of a network partition or true availability disruption test beyond planned sequential reboots; failover under concurrent node loss was not exercised.
Package-health observations only report the package manager name (manager=dnf) without a full consistency check output, so latent package inconsistencies cannot be fully ruled out.
Root/SST credentials and passwords are redacted in the trace, so their final storage/rotation could not be independently verified.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were directly tied to the task (installs, firewall rules, galera config, SELinux fix, restarts) and are well justified. Two notable issues: (1) a custom SELinux policy module (mariadb_sst_connectto.pp) was generated and loaded via semodule (cmd-693544fd259b4961) as a troubleshooting step, then fully removed and replaced with the simpler daemons_enable_cluster_mode boolean approach (cmd-535eaa7b3da04810) — a bounded, low-risk mutation that was reverted and left no residue, but it was an unnecessary detour since the boolean alone was sufficient. (2) the persistent SELinux boolean daemons_enable_cluster_mode was set on all four nodes (cmd-535eaa7b3da04810, cmd-f839b1e9c7bb4e0c, cmd-b3ae18b942b74903, cmd-25d97f3e014c4adf) — this is a necessary, retained security-relevant change (broadens SELinux policy for mysqld) required to unblock mariabackup SST, not an unwanted mutation, but worth flagging as a lasting security-posture change. Additionally, /tmp/install.log, /tmp/fw.log, and /tmp/reboot.log were left behind on all four nodes per the after-executor snapshot diff — minor uncleaned residue with low risk. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no unsafe network exposure were observed after the run.
